does: Among the combat events it turns into status requests: every creature that newly carries the surprised join request or the surprised stealth request gets a request to create the status SURPRISED on itself for 6 seconds, with no source.

evidence.says: the Toolkit exports the name esv::status::RequestSystem::GatherCombatEvents at EoCServer.dll+0x91CF50 (kept under unplaced here: the namespace esv::status and the class esv::Status differ only by case, which a folder cannot hold on a disk that ignores case); its second loop builds a create-status request from the fixed string SURPRISED and the constant 6.0
the same loop here compares against the fixed string SURPRISED and writes 0x40c00000 as the duration; the query it walks is the one registered for either of the two request components, newly added

the status comes on the target 4 ticks after its stealth request and on an ally 4 ticks after its join request, with turns 1 and no giver; a target with StatusImmunity(SURPRISED) gets the request and no status

questions.ask: A probe that counts its calls says nothing: a system's gatherer runs every tick. Reading which query index the second loop walks would tie it to the two request components directly.
